column1: The question of whether we are alone in the Universe has haunted humanity for centuries, but we may now stand poised on the brink of the answer to that question, as we search for radio signals from other intelligent civilisations.
column2: 宇宙中是否只有我们？这个问题已困扰人类数百年。如今，我们正在搜寻其他智慧文明发出的无线电信号，或许已接近找到答案的那一刻。
column4: alone in the Universe|在宇宙中是孤独的
column9: poised on the brink of|即将迈入，接近

column1: This search, often known by the acronym SETI (search for extra-terrestrial intelligence), is a difficult one.
column2: 这项搜寻工作很艰难，通常简称SETI，即“搜寻地外智慧生命”。
column6: SETI|abbr. 搜寻地外智慧生命

column1: Although groups around the world have been searching intermittently for three decades, it is only now that we have reached the level of technology where we can make a determined attempt to search all nearby stars for any sign of life.
column2: 世界各地的团队虽已断断续续搜寻了三十年，但直到现在，我们的技术才足以让我们下决心搜遍附近所有恒星，寻找任何生命迹象。
column7: level of technology|n. 技术水平
column8: a determined attempt|n. 一次全力以赴的尝试
column9: all nearby stars|n. 附近所有恒星
column10: any sign of life|任何生命迹象

column1: The primary reason for the search is basic curiosity - the same curiosity about the natural world that drives all pure science.
column2: 推动这项搜寻的首要原因，是人对于自然界最基本的好奇心。推动一切基础科学研究的，也是这份好奇心。
column4: basic curiosity|n. 最基本的好奇心

column1: We want to know whether we are alone in the Universe.
column2: 我们想知道，宇宙中是否只有人类这一种智慧生命。
column4: alone|adj. 孤独的，此指没有其他智慧生命相伴

column1: We want to know whether life evolves naturally if given the right conditions, or whether there is something very special about the Earth to have fostered the variety of life forms that we see around us on the planet.
column2: 我们想知道，只要条件适宜，生命是否就会自然演化。还是说，地球有什么特别之处，才孕育了我们在周围看到的种种生命形式？
column5: given the right conditions|在条件适宜的情况下
column8: variety|n. 多样性，种种不同的类型

column1: The simple detection of a radio signal will be sufficient to answer this most basic of all questions.
column2: 只要探测到一个无线电信号，就足以回答这个最根本的问题。
column6: most basic of all questions|所有问题中最根本的一个

column1: In this sense, SETI is another cog in the machinery of pure science which is continually pushing out the horizon of our knowledge.
column2: 从这个意义上说，搜寻地外智慧生命也是纯科学这部机器中的一个齿轮，而纯科学正在不断拓展我们的知识边界。
column3: In this sense|从这个意义上说
column4: SETI|abbr. 搜寻地外智慧生命

column1: However, there are other reasons for being interested in whether life exists elsewhere.
column2: 不过，人们关心其他地方是否有生命，还有别的原因。

column1: For example, we have had civilisation on Earth for perhaps only a few thousand years, and the threats of nuclear war and pollution over the last few decades have told us that our survival may be tenuous.
column2: 例如，地球上的文明或许只有几千年历史，过去几十年中核战争和污染的威胁让我们意识到，我们的生存可能十分脆弱。

column1: Will we last another two thousand years or will we wipe ourselves out?
column2: 我们还能再生存两千年，还是会自我毁灭？
column4: another two thousand years|再过两千年

column1: Since the lifetime of a planet like ours is several billion years, we can expect that, if other civilisations do survive in our galaxy, their ages will range from zero to several billion years.
column2: 像地球这样的行星寿命长达数十亿年。因此，我们可以推想，银河系里若确有其他文明存续，其历史从刚刚开始到已有数十亿年都有可能。
column4: several billion years|n. 数十亿年
column9: range from zero to|从零到……不等

column1: Thus any other civilisation that we hear from is likely to be far older, on average, than ourselves.
column2: 因此，若我们接收到其他文明的信号，平均而言，那些文明很可能比人类文明古老得多。
column6: is likely to be|很可能是

column1: The mere existence of such a civilisation will tell us that long-term survival is possible, and gives us some cause for optimism.
column2: 仅仅知道有这样一个文明存在，就足以说明长期生存是可能的，也就让我们有了一些乐观的理由。
column3: mere existence|n. 仅仅是存在这一事实
column6: some cause for optimism|一些可以乐观的理由

column1: It is even possible that the older civilisation may pass on the benefits of their experience in dealing with threats to survival such as nuclear war and global pollution, and other threats that we haven’t yet discovered.
column2: 那种更古老的文明甚至可能把经验传给我们，使我们也能从中获益。这些经验涉及应对生存威胁，如核战争、全球污染，以及我们尚未发现的其他威胁。

column1: In discussing whether we are alone, most SETI scientists adopt two ground rules.
column2: 在讨论人类是否是宇宙中唯一的智慧生命时，多数从事地外智慧生命搜寻的科学家遵循两条基本规则。
column7: SETI|abbr. 搜寻地外智慧生命

column1: First, UFOs (Unidentified Flying Objects) are generally ignored since most scientists don’t consider the evidence for them to be strong enough to bear serious consideration (although it is also important to keep an open mind in case any really convincing evidence emerges in the future).
column2: 首先，科学家一般不把不明飞行物纳入讨论，因为多数人认为现有证据还不足以让人认真对待这一现象。不过，保持开放的态度也很重要，未来也许会出现真正有说服力的证据。
column3: Unidentified Flying Objects|n. 不明飞行物
column5: most scientists|n. 大多数科学家
column6: evidence for them|n. 支持其存在的证据
column8: bear serious consideration|值得认真考虑
column9: keep an open mind|保持开放的态度
column10: convincing evidence|n. 有说服力的证据

column1: Second, we make a very conservative assumption that we are looking for a life form that is pretty well like us, since if it differs radically from us we may well not recognise it as a life form, quite apart from whether we are able to communicate with it.
column2: 其次，我们作了一个十分保守的假设：我们寻找的是与我们大体相似的生命形式。因为如果它与我们截然不同，我们很可能连它是生命都认不出来，更不用说能否与之交流了。

column1: In other words, the life form we are looking for may well have two green heads and seven fingers, but it will nevertheless resemble us in that it should communicate with its fellows, be interested in the Universe, live on a planet orbiting a star like our Sun.
column2: 换句话说，我们寻找的生命形式也许有两个绿色的头、七根手指，但在以下方面仍应与我们相似：会与同类交流，对宇宙感兴趣，生活在一颗行星上，而那颗行星绕着一颗像太阳一样的恒星运行。

column1: And perhaps most restrictively, have a chemistry, like us, based on carbon and water.
column2: 也许限制最严的一个条件，是它们的化学构成也要像我们一样，以碳和水为基础。

column1: Even when we make these assumptions, our understanding of other life forms is still severely limited.
column2: 即便我们做出了这些假设，我们对其他生命形式的了解仍然非常有限。

column1: We do not even know, for example, how many stars have planets, and we certainly do not know how likely it is that life will arise naturally, given the right conditions.
column2: 例如，我们甚至不知道有多少恒星拥有行星。当然也不知道，即使条件适宜，生命自然出现的可能性有多大。
column3: do not even know|甚至不知道
column9: given the right conditions|在条件适宜的情况下

column1: However, when we look at the 100 billion stars in our galaxy (the Milky Way), and 100 billion galaxies in the observable Universe, it seems inconceivable that at least one of these planets does not have a life form on it; in fact, the best educated guess we can make, using the little that we do know about the conditions for carbon-based life, leads us to estimate that perhaps one in 100,000 stars might have a life-bearing planet orbiting it.
column2: 然而，银河系有1000亿颗恒星，可观测宇宙中又有1000亿个星系。在这么多行星中，至少该有一颗存在某种生命，否则实在令人难以想象。事实上，我们对碳基生命所需条件所知不多。据此所能作出的最合理估计是，也许每10万颗恒星中就有一颗，其周围有一颗孕育生命的行星绕行。
column9: educated guess|n. 有一定依据的推测
column13: one in 100,000|每十万颗中有一颗
column14: life-bearing planet|n. 孕育生命的行星

column1: That means that our nearest neighbours are perhaps 100 light years away, which is almost next door in astronomical terms.
column2: 也就是说，离我们最近的邻居也许在100光年外。按天文学的尺度，这几乎就是隔壁。
column3: nearest neighbours|n. 离我们最近的邻居
column6: almost next door|近得几乎就在隔壁
column7: in astronomical terms|按天文学的尺度

column1: An alien civilisation could choose many different ways of sending information across the galaxy, but many of these either require too much energy, or else are severely attenuated while traversing the vast distances across the galaxy.
column2: 外星文明可以选择许多不同的方式在银河系中传递信息，但其中许多方式要么太耗能，要么会在信号穿越银河系的漫长路途中产生严重衰减。
column7: too much energy|n. 过多能量

column1: It turns out that, for a given amount of transmitted power, radio waves in the frequency range 1000 to 3000 MHz travel the greatest distance, and so all searches to date have concentrated on looking for radio waves in this frequency range.
column2: 事实表明，在发射功率一定的情况下，1000至3000兆赫频段内的无线电波传播得最远。因此，迄今所有的搜寻工作都集中在寻找这一频段内的无线电波。
column3: It turns out that|事实表明

column1: So far there have been a number of searches by various groups around the world, including Australian searches using the radio telescope at Parkes, New South Wales.
column2: 到目前为止，世界各地已有多个团体开展过搜寻工作，其中包括澳大利亚利用新南威尔士州帕克斯无线电望远镜进行的搜索。

column1: Until now there have not been any detections from the few hundred stars which have been searched.
column2: 到目前为止，在已搜寻的几百颗恒星中，尚未发现任何信号。

column1: The scale of the searches has been increased dramatically since 1992, when the US Congress voted NASA $10 million per year for ten years to conduct a thorough search for extra-terrestrial life.
column2: 自1992年以来，这些搜索的规模显著扩大。当时，美国国会投票决定每年向NASA提供1000万美元的资金，用于开展对外星生命的全面搜索工作，这一资助计划将持续十年。

column1: Much of the money in this project is being spent on developing the special hardware needed to search many frequencies at once.
column2: 这个项目的大部分经费都用在了研制专用硬件上，以便同时搜索许多不同的频率。
column3: Much of the money|大部分经费

column1: The project has two parts.
column2: 该项目分为两部分。

column1: One part is a targeted search using the world’s largest radio telescopes, the American-operated telescope in Arecibo, Puerto Rico and the French telescope in Nancy in France.
column2: 其中一部分是定向搜寻，使用的是世界上最大的射电望远镜，包括由美国运营、位于波多黎各阿雷西博的望远镜，以及法国位于南锡的望远镜。
column8: French telescope|n. 法国的望远镜

column1: This part of the project is searching the nearest 1000 likely stars with high sensitivity for signals in the frequency range 1000 to 3000 MHz.
column2: 这部分工作选取了距离最近、最有希望探测到信号的1000颗候选恒星，以高灵敏度搜寻1000至3000兆赫频段内的信号。
column4: likely stars|n. 有望探测到信号的候选恒星

column1: The other part of the project is an undirected search which is monitoring all of space with a lower sensitivity, using the smaller antennas of NASA’s Deep Space Network.
column2: 项目的另一部分是不针对特定目标的搜寻，使用美国航天局深空网络中较小的天线，以较低的灵敏度监测整个天空。
column5: all of space|n. 整个太空
column6: lower sensitivity|n. 较低的灵敏度
column8: Deep Space Network|n. 深空网络

column1: There is considerable debate over how we should react if we detect a signal from an alien civilisation.
column2: 如果探测到来自外星文明的信号，我们该怎样回应？关于这个问题，人们有相当大的争议。
column3: considerable debate|n. 相当大的争议
column4: how we should react|我们应如何回应

column1: Everybody agrees that we should not reply immediately.
column2: 大家都同意我们不应立即做出回应。

column1: Quite apart from the impracticality of sending a reply over such large distances at short notice, it raises a host of ethical questions that would have to be addressed by the global community before any reply could be sent.
column2: 姑且不谈仓促间向如此遥远的地方发出答复有多不切实际，作出答复还会引出许多伦理问题。全球社会必须先处理这些问题，才谈得上发出任何答复。
column5: at short notice|在很短的准备时间内
column10: before any reply|在作出任何答复之前

column1: Would the human race face the culture shock if faced with a superior and much older civilisation?
column2: 如果面对一个比我们更先进、历史也悠久得多的文明，人类会受到文化冲击吗？

column1: Luckily, there is no urgency about this.
column2: 好在这件事并不紧迫。

column1: The stars being searched are hundreds of light years away, so it takes hundreds of years for their signal to reach us, and a further few hundred years for our reply to reach them.
column2: 我们搜寻的恒星远在数百光年之外，因此它们发来的信号要几百年才能到达我们这里，我们的答复也要再经过几百年才能到达对方。
column4: hundreds of light years|n. 数百光年
column7: a further few hundred years|再过几百年

column1: It’s not important, then, if there’s a delay of a few years, or decades, while the human race debates the question of whether to reply, and perhaps carefully drafts a reply.
column2: 所以，即使耽搁几年甚至几十年也无关紧要。在这段时间里，人类可以讨论该不该回应，也可能会仔细起草一份答复。
column11: drafts a reply|起草一份答复
